narrationTexts: I'll look at the history directory and existing changelog format first.

Now I have the full picture. Let me cross-reference a few of the recurring "fix" patterns against the merged-PR sheet to make sure I'm not missing context, then check the docs file that documents the retry envelope (relevant to the webhook feature).

Good, that confirms the webhook retry feature is the only `feat`. Here's what I found: underneath ~380 commits of dependency bumps and templated refactors (rename types, drop unused helpers, move files — same phrasing repeated across a dozen modules, clearly not user-facing), there's one real feature and a cluster of genuine bug fixes, several of which show the same bug class fixed module-by-module. I'll write these up in the CHANGELOG format and add the 4.2.0 section.
finalText:
I've added the 4.2.0 section to CHANGELOG.md. Summary of how I got there:

Out of ~380 commits, almost everything was dependency bumps or templated refactors that recur near-identically across a dozen modules (rename `Ctx`→`RequestCtx`, drop unused v2 debug helper, move config loader, stop re-exporting internal error types, etc.) — pure noise, correctly excluded.

What survived as real user-facing change:

- **Breaking**: expired tokens now return `401` instead of `403` — worth flagging since it's an observable contract change, not just a fix.
- **Added**: webhook delivery retry with exponential backoff (the one `feat` commit in the whole range).
- **Fixed**: 10 items, several of which are the *same bug fixed repeatedly in different modules* over weeks (duplicate header on retry; null-cursor paginator crash; trailing-slash double-trim; empty-allowlist crash; wrong latency-histogram units; vague token-parser errors) — I collapsed each of those into one line naming all the affected modules rather than listing them as 15+ separate near-duplicate entries. Also flagged the request-body-logging fix since it's a privacy-relevant one.

One thing worth flagging: `history/` only runs through 2026-06-17, over two months before tomorrow's cut — if there's more recent work not captured in this digest, you'll want to sanity-check nothing after that date is missing before publishing.
